errors.text_span: This pie chart presents the distribution of clustering results for the FineWeb-Edu Classifier
errors.evidence: The image contains two separate charts, "AttentionInfluence" and "FineWeb-Edu Classifier". The description incorrectly treats them as a single chart, referencing only the "FineWeb-Edu Classifier" in the opening but then listing categories from both.
The description states the chart has 28 slices. This is incorrect. The left chart ("AttentionInfluence") has 21 slices and the right chart ("FineWeb-Edu Classifier") has 20 slices.
The description claims to be about the "FineWeb-Edu Classifier" chart, but the category "Policy" only appears in the "AttentionInfluence" chart.
The description omits the prominent red/pink color used for several slices in both charts (e.g., 'Science', 'Animal & Plant').
The description misinterprets the numerical values in the slices as percentages. The labels are integer counts (e.g., 19, 17, 38), not percentages.

errors.text_span: the largest slice being “Science & technology education”
errors.evidence: In the 'FineWeb-Edu Classifier' chart, the largest slice is 'Education' with a value of 38, not 'Science & technology education' with a value of 19.
The slice for 'Education' has a value of 38. The value 17 corresponds to the 'Teaching & resources' slice.
The slice for 'Healthy education' has a value of 2. The value 15 corresponds to the 'Science' slice.

errors.text_span: “Historical review” is represented by a prominent, exploded slice
errors.evidence: No slices in the chart are exploded or offset. This is a hallucinated feature.

errors.text_span: and “Events & people” is visually emphasized, appearing offset from the other slices
errors.evidence: The 'Events & people' slice is not offset from the other slices. This is a hallucinated visual feature.

errors.text_span: while all other slices contain percentage labels within them
errors.evidence: This is an over-generalization. Several of the smallest slices in the inner rings have their labels placed outside the chart with pointers, not within the slice.

errors.text_span: The slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest in terms of their angular size.
errors.evidence: The slices are not ordered by size. For instance, in the teal group of the right-hand chart, the values are 38, 17, 19, and 2, which is not a descending order.
